messages.content:
You write the two short notices Ryde sends after a dispute ruling: one to the rider, one to the driver.
Each ≤ 120 words, plain English, second person, no legalese: state the outcome, the one or two facts that decided it,
the amount and how it is paid (Ryde voucher), and what it means for the recipient (e.g. account review). Do not cite
ids like F3 or RD-2. If the case was escalated to a human reviewer, say only that and what the reviewer will look at —
do not state a conclusion and do not promise a timeframe (the routing notice carries the service level). Return JSON: {"rider": "...", "driver": "..."}

Case B-0001. Final outcome: refund_partial, amount $4.33 as a Ryde voucher. Account flag: no. Recommended action: Issue a $4.33 voucher refund to the rider (RydeTAXI metered-fare overcharge), and remind the driver that unexplained off-route mileage is a breach of the shortest-and-most-direct obligation..
Reasoning:
RD-1: the trip is RydeTAXI (metered), so extra kilometres enter the fare directly; the GPS record shows one unexplained off-route segment 09:24–09:30, 3.78 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, +3.07 km and up to 688 m off the optimal route [F3], and no exemption applies, so the segment is refundable under RD-2 [F3][RD-1].

RD-4: no incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F13]; the only congestion evidence is speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard [F11][F12], which is outside RD-4(b)'s band 1–2, and band evidence is corroborative only (G3). With no RD-4(a) incident the segment falls to RD-2 treatment [F11][F12][F13][RD-4].

RD-5: the driver's post-trip statement "I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted" is not rider consent and, appearing only in his own statement, cannot exempt the segment (G11) [F10]. The chat is complete and timestamped: a 09:04 rider pickup note and a 09:05 driver "2 min away," with no route discussion before the segment started at 09:24 [F7][F8][F9]; the trace timestamps the segment start at 09:24:50, so no rider message sent before 09:24:50 agrees to anything. A complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment counts; the trace also notes no stop was measured, so RD-3 gives no exemption either [F3][F7][F8][F9][RD-5].

Amount (RD-2): the refund is the unexempted segment's extra kilometres priced at this trip's own per-km rate, which the fare record supplies as distance fare ÷ distance km = $34.42 ÷ 24.41 km = $1.41008/km [F6]. $1.41008/km × 3.07 km (extra_km in [F3]) = $4.3290, rounded to $4.33. The billed excess line of 3.20 km is a separate figure covering the whole-trip excess; RD-2 refunds only the segment's extra_km and expressly does not refund mileage outside any segment, so the award is computed from [F3], not from the 3.20 km in [F4] [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].

RD-6: the driver's 90-day profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F16], so the "repeated" route-deviation predicate is absent and no flag_account attaches; the profile facts (F15, F16) carry neither side's finding [F15][F16][RD-6].

function.name: final_result
function.description: The final response which ends this conversation

function.name: final_result
function.arguments:
{"rider": "We reviewed your dispute and are refunding $4.33 as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: your RydeTAXI fare is metered, so extra distance goes straight into what you pay. The GPS record shows one unexplained off-route stretch during your trip — 3.78 km driven where the direct route was 0.71 km. Nothing excused that detour: no incident or serious congestion was recorded on the route, and the app chat shows you never agreed to a different route.

The $4.33 covers just that stretch's extra kilometres, at your trip's own per-kilometre rate, and will be credited to your Ryde voucher balance. No action is needed on your account.", "driver": "We reviewed this trip and are refunding the rider $4.33 as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: this was a metered RydeTAXI trip, so extra distance is charged directly to the rider. The GPS record shows one stretch where you drove 3.78 km while the direct route was 0.71 km, and nothing excused it — no recorded incident or significant congestion on the route, and no rider agreement to a different route in the app chat. Going where the app sent you isn't consent from the rider.

Please keep to the shortest and most direct route. This is a reminder only; no flag was placed on your account."}
